original_question: Determine whether every contracted modular numerical semigroup admits a Toms decomposition.
target_in_paper: Section 3 (“The quotient of a numerical semigroup by a positive integer”): the paper restates the conjecture as “It is conjectured in [57] that every contracted modular numerical semigroup admits a Toms decomposition.”
correct_elements: Your draft captures the exact mathematical target of the paper almost verbatim: the quantified class is “every contracted modular numerical semigroup,” and the property is “admits a Toms decomposition.” This is precisely the conjecture singled out in the Section 3 discussion. You also avoid drifting to the broader neighboring question about replacing proportionally modular systems by modular ones.
missing_details: Specify the ambient object: a numerical semigroup is a subset S of N={0,1,2,...} that is closed under addition, contains 0, and has finite complement in N.
Define “contracted modular numerical semigroup” explicitly: S=T(a,b,c)∪{0} for some a,b,c in N with b>0, where T(a,b,c)={x in N : ax mod b <= x-c}.
State what “ax mod b” means: the least nonnegative remainder of ax modulo b.
Make explicit that, in this context, no extra hypotheses on a,b,c are imposed beyond a,c being nonnegative and b being positive.

Define “admits a Toms decomposition” in a stand-alone way; in this paper one may do so via the proved equivalent characterization that S is a finite intersection of proportionally modular numerical semigroups.
If the equivalent characterization is used, define each proportionally modular component as a semigroup of the form {x in N : a_i x mod b_i <= c_i x} for suitable coefficients in the paper’s sense.
Indicate that this is an open conjectural problem in the paper, not a theorem or proved characterization.
Separate this conjecture from the immediately following broader question asking whether every system of proportionally modular inequalities can be replaced by one with all proportions equal to 1.
refined_question: Let N={0,1,2,...}. If S⊆N is a numerical semigroup of the form S={0}∪{x∈N : (ax mod b) <= x-c} for some a,b,c∈N with b>0, where ax mod b denotes the least nonnegative remainder of ax modulo b, must S admit a Toms decomposition; equivalently in the sense used in the paper, must S be expressible as a finite intersection of proportionally modular numerical semigroups?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does every contracted modular numerical semigroup S={0}∪{x∈N : (ax mod b) <= x-c} admit a representation S=⋂_{i=1}^r {x∈N : (a_i x mod b_i) <= c_i x} for some finite r and suitable coefficients defining proportionally modular Diophantine inequalities?
justification: The draft matches the specific conjecture isolated in the paper’s Section 3. The nearby context first defines contracted modular numerical semigroups, then recalls that admitting a Toms decomposition is equivalent to being a finite intersection of proportionally modular numerical semigroups, and only after that states the exact conjecture. The refined version therefore keeps the scope exactly at that conjecture, while making all hidden definitions explicit and avoiding the broader subsequent question about intersections of modular numerical semigroups.
